title: Mates of pasted squares and of conjugate-whiskered squares
statement:
Notation of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: for adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1$ ($L_1:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$), $L_2\dashv R_2$ ($L_2:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$) and functors $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$, a *square* is a natural transformation $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and $\alpha^\flat:GR_1\to R_2H$ is its mate; conjugates $\tau^c$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

1. (Pasting along $G,H$.) Let moreover $L_3\dashv R_3$ ($L_3:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$), $G_2:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, $H_2:\mathcal D\to\mathcal F$, $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and $\beta:L_3G_2\to H_2L_2$. The pasted square $\gamma=(H_2\alpha)\circ(\beta G):L_3G_2G\to H_2HL_1$ has mate $\gamma^\flat=(\beta^\flat H)\circ(G_2\alpha^\flat):G_2GR_1\to G_2R_2H\to R_3H_2H$.
2. (Pasting along the adjunctions.) Let $L_1\dashv R_1$ ($\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$), $L_3\dashv R_3$ ($\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$), $L_2\dashv R_2$ ($\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$), $L_4\dashv R_4$ ($\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$), $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$, $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$, $K:\mathcal C\to\mathcal F$, $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$, $\beta:L_4H\to KL_3$. With respect to the composite adjunctions $L_3L_1\dashv R_1R_3$ and $L_4L_2\dashv R_2R_4$ (unit $R_1\eta_3L_1\circ\eta_1$, counit $\varepsilon_3\circ L_3\varepsilon_1R_3$), the pasted square $\delta=(\beta L_1)\circ(L_4\alpha):L_4L_2G\to KL_3L_1$ has mate $\delta^\flat=(R_2\beta^\flat)\circ(\alpha^\flat R_3):GR_1R_3\to R_2HR_3\to R_2R_4K$.
3. (Changing the adjunctions by a transformation.) (a) For a square $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and a third adjunction $L_3\dashv R_3$ with $L_3:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $\tau:L_3\to L_2$, the square $\alpha\circ(\tau G):L_3G\to HL_1$ has mate (for $L_1\dashv R_1$, $L_3\dashv R_3$) equal to $(\tau^cH)\circ\alpha^\flat:GR_1\to R_2H\to R_3H$, $\tau^c:R_2\to R_3$. (b) For an adjunction $L_0\dashv R_0$ with $L_0:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $\sigma:L_1\to L_0$, and a square $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$, the square $(H\sigma)\circ\alpha:L_2G\to HL_0$ has mate (for $L_0\dashv R_0$, $L_2\dashv R_2$) equal to $\alpha^\flat\circ(G\sigma^c):GR_0\to GR_1\to R_2H$, $\sigma^c:R_0\to R_1$.
4. (Identity.) For one adjunction $L\dashv R$ and $G,H$ identity functors, the mate of $\mathrm{id}_L$ is $\mathrm{id}_R$.
